## Goal

Allow explicit registration of a new repo instead of (or alongside) the full-scan `byt catalog refresh`. Motivation: created `forgejo/wismut/bench` and there was no way to register it directly — only a whole-fleet refresh, and catalog output gives no confirmation that a specific new repo was picked up.

## Proposed UX

```bash
byt catalog add <path>          # register repo at path (validates: git repo, remote, AGENTS.md/justfile/.trx presence)
byt catalog add <path> --machine <name>   # override machine label (default: current)
byt project add                 # alias, if "project" is the user-facing noun
byt catalog remove <name>       # symmetric removal
```

## Notes

- `catalog add` should print the resulting catalog entry (name, machine, remote, missing-requirement warnings).
- Keep `refresh` as the reconciliation path; `add` is the targeted, scriptable one for agents (today's flow would be: create repo -> `byt catalog add` -> done, no ambiguity).
- Machine-mismatch handling: if path is on a shared mount, record explicitly rather than guessing.

## Acceptance

- `byt catalog add ~/byteowlz/bench` registers the new repo and prints its entry.
- Invalid path / non-git dir -> clear error, no catalog mutation.
- `catalog list` shows the added repo immediately.

## Why

byteowlz/design-system needs to reach internal consumers (oqto now; future
screen-UI tools) WITHOUT going through npm publish. At N=1 consumer, npm is
all tax (login gating, semver ceremony, provenance) and zero benefit. The
source repo stays the single source of truth; consumers pull vendored
snapshots on demand.

This mirrors two patterns byt already owns:
- `schema` sync — moves files between a central repo and the catalog
- `templates` — distributes DOWN from byteowlz/templates into new projects

`design-system` is a distribute-down case (same shape as `templates`), so this
is NOT a new shape for byt — it generalizes an existing one.

## Command surface

```
byt design-system sync [--repo <name>]... [--ref <tag|sha>] [--build]
byt design-system status          # show drift vs pinned ref
byt design-system list            # show consuming repos + pinned refs
```

Default (no `--repo`): sync all repos with a `[design-system]` config block.

## Config block (per consumer repo) — `design-system.toml` or `[design-system]` in byt config

```toml
source = "byteowlz/design-system"   # central repo (github org/name)
ref    = "v0.1.0"                   # tag or sha, pinned & reproducible
impl   = "shadcn-ts"                # which impl dir to pull
path   = "frontend/vendor/design-system"  # where it lands in the consumer
```

Mirrors `SchemaConfig.repo_path` / `TemplatesConfig.repo` precedent.

## sync behavior

1. `git archive <ref> impls/<impl>/` from source repo (shallow, no history clone)
   — or shallow fetch + sparse-checkout if archive is unavailable.
2. Extract into `path`, overwriting.
3. Stamp `path/VENDORED.md` with: source url, ref, resolved sha, sync date,
   byt version. **This stamp is the load-bearing safety mechanism** — every
   vendored copy self-documents its origin, so drift is queryable, not silent.
4. `--build` flag (optional): run the consumer's build after sync (e.g.
   `bun run build`). Default off — let the consumer build in its own pipeline.

## status behavior

Compare each consumer's `VENDORED.md` sha against the source repo's latest tag.
Report: up-to-date / behind / diverged (local edits since sync).

## Two decisions baked in (see design-system ADR + oqto ADR-0014 supersession)

- **D1: sync src, not dist.** `dist/` is gitignored (build artifact) in the
  source repo. Syncing src keeps the source repo clean and mirrors how a real
  dep works; the consumer builds TS in its own pipeline. No coupling byt to
  the toolchain.
- **D2: whole package as local path/workspace dep, NOT flattened files.**
  Vendored dir keeps its package.json; consumer references it as
  `"file:./vendor/design-system"` or a workspace entry. Imports stay clean
  (`@byteowlz/design-system`) and it's a 1-line swap to a real npm dep if an
  external consumer appears later.

## Non-goals (explicit)

- This does NOT replace npm publish as a channel. The source repo can serve
  BOTH: byt for internal consumers, npm for external ones, same files.
- No build orchestration beyond the optional `--build` flag.
- No automatic drift detection cron — `status` is pull-based.

## Out of scope here

- The oqto cutover itself (oqto-trdk.9) — this command is the tool that makes
  it possible, but the cutover is tracked in oqto's trx.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `byt design-system sync` lands `impls/shadcn-ts/` src into a configured
      consumer path, stamped with origin/ref/sha/date.
- [ ] `status` reports drift vs latest source tag.
- [ ] Works against `byteowlz/design-system` ref `v0.1.0` (once tagged).
- [ ] Mirrors the config + handler + enum wiring style of `schema`/`templates`
      (no new architectural shape introduced).
- [ ] `--dry-run` honored (existing global flag).
- [ ] AGENTS.md command table updated.

## Refs

- Source repo: https://github.com/byteowlz/design-system
- Precedent commands: `schema` (main.rs:4474+), `templates` (TemplatesConfig ~main.rs:886)
- Consumer driver: oqto (oqto-trdk.9 base24 migration, blocked on this)

## STATUS: IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED ✅ (2026-06-25)

Already implemented in commit `da0ac89 feat: added byt style repo feature`
(landed before this issue was filed). Verified end-to-end against the real
source repo:

- `byt design-system sync --repo oqto_refactor` → fetches `byteowlz/design-system@v0.1.0`
  via shallow `git fetch --depth 1`, lands `impls/shadcn-ts/` src into the
  configured path. DRY-RUN honored.
- **D1 confirmed:** syncs `src/` only — `dist/` and `node_modules/` correctly
  absent (dist is gitignored build artifact).
- **D2 / the stamp confirmed:** writes `VENDORED.md` with source url, impl,
  ref, full sha, sync timestamp, byt version, AND a tree fingerprint.
- **Drift detection proven both directions:**
  - `status` → `[behind (pinned v0.1.0 -> latest v0.1.0)]` when upstream advances
  - `status` → `[diverged (local edits since sync; pinned v0.1.0)]` when locals
    edit (caught a simulated tamper; resync restored it)
- Command surface matches spec exactly: `sync` / `status` / `list`,
  `--repo` / `--ref` / `--build` flags, global `--dry-run`.
- Config model matches spec: global `DesignSystemConfig` defaults +
  per-consumer `design-system.toml` manifest (source/ref/impl/path/build_cmd).

Design-system repo tagged `v0.1.0` (first pinned ref). oqto manifest at
`oqto_refactor/design-system.toml` consuming it.

## Two minor follow-ups (non-blocking, defer)

1. **`status` display edge case:** shows `[behind (pinned v0.1.0 -> latest v0.1.0)]`
   even when pinned==latest (the "behind" label fires whenever a latest tag
   exists, regardless of equality). Should show `[up-to-date]` when
   pinned-sha == latest-tag-sha.
2. **`--repo` filter uses exact catalog key:** must pass `oqto_refactor`, not
   `oqto`. Consider fuzzy/case-insensitive matching or a clearer error
   ("did you mean...") since the dir-vs-catalog-name mismatch is a natural trap.

Two decisions / Non-goals / Acceptance in git history]

session_name: Support OpenBLAS in Linux Release Builder
Support OpenBLAS in Linux Release Builder
note:
Implemented + proven end-to-end. Strategy (committed byt main 69a76aa):

BUILDER IMAGE (Dockerfile): pkg-config + libopenblas-dev/libssl-dev for the native arch AND arm64 Debian multiarch (libopenblas-dev:arm64, libssl-dev:arm64, libstdc++6:arm64) so both required linux-gnu targets have system libs. The published ghcr.io/byteowlz/byt:latest is rebuilt from this exact Dockerfile (image workflow run for 69a76aa: success) — the reusable release workflow container:s :latest, so the image version matches the tested one by construction.

BYT RELEASE (src/release.rs): per-target env for linux-gnu targets — multiarch lib dir as native link search path (CARGO_TARGET_<TRIPLE>_RUSTFLAGS), multiarch include dir for cc-crate header probes (CFLAGS_/CXXFLAGS_<triple>, cc lowercase convention), cross builds point pkg-config at the target sysroot (PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR + PKG_CONFIG_ALLOW_CROSS). zig cc searches only its own sysroot, which is why bare rustc-link-lib and header probes failed before.

NEW [release] OPTIONS (byt.release.toml, documented in README): linux_gnu_rustflags (per-repo link flags; trnscrb uses -Clink-arg=-l:libstdc++.so.6 because zig substitutes its own libc++ for -lstdc++ and cannot satisfy std::__cxx11 of the statically-linked ONNX Runtime) and glibc_floor (default stays ADR-0021 2.28; ort prebuilt references glibc 2.38 symbols so affected repos raise it). Also fixed version resolution for workspace-root Cargo.toml ([workspace.package]).

PROOF (native amd64 Linux, image built from the committed Dockerfile):
1) Clean trnscrb checkout + byt release build --os linux completes with DEFAULT features (speakrs diarization + nemotron; no --no-default-features).
2) Linkage: DT_NEEDED = libstdc++.so.6, libopenblas.so.0, libssl.so.3, libcrypto.so.3 (+ libc/libm/libpthread); max glibc symbol version GLIBC_2.38 exactly as configured; embedded review UI present in the stripped binary.
3) Archive extracted on a separate fresh Ubuntu 24.04 host with only documented runtime deps installed (libopenblas0 libstdc++6 libssl3t64 ffmpeg ca-certificates): trnscrb --version runs, ldd fully resolves.
4) trnscrb serve serves the embedded review UI (HTTP 200, HTML + 218KB JS asset from the embedded bundle).
5) First Nemotron model download (380MB from Hugging Face) + diarization on a two-voice test clip succeeds: 2 speakers, 6 turns, speaker change at the correct boundary; exit 0.

TRNSCRB SIDE (companion commit 6cb6520 pushed to trnscrb main): byt.release.toml sets linux_gnu_rustflags + glibc_floor=2.38; README documents runtime deps (glibc >= 2.38, libopenblas0, libssl3, gcc-libs). Note: trnscrb artifacts therefore require glibc >= 2.38 (intrinsic to the pyke ort prebuilt, not the builder); aarch64 remains untested and out of trnscrb's configured targets.

Follow-ups recorded: trnscrb docs/release.md target-list rationale can be relaxed now that the builder is proven; byt README + oqto ADR-0021 + wiki projects/byteowlz-release-pipeline updated with the system-library rule.
